county.name: Langlade County Forest
county.short: Berries, fruit, nuts, mushrooms and edible plants for your own use. No permit.
limits: Mushrooms: 1 lb total in your possession
More than that needs a commercial permit
never: Anything for sale without a permit
county.motor: Cars and trucks only on county forest roads not closed by signs, gates or barriers. ATVs/UTVs only on roads and trails open to them; no off-trail riding.
county.hours: Developed recreation sites and day-use areas close 10 p.m. to 7 a.m.
county.cite: Langlade County Code ch. 16, Forest, Parks and Recreation Ordinance, ss. 16.02(30)-(32), 16.06(3)(c), 16.06(4)(a), 16.06(16), 16.06(29)

state.name: State land (DNR wildlife, fishery and natural areas)
state.short: Only edible fruits, edible nuts, wild mushrooms, wild asparagus and watercress, by hand, for your own eating.
limits: Personal consumption only, not for sale
never: Greens, shoots and roots such as ramps, fiddleheads, nettles or cattail
Seeds and other plant parts without a permit
state.motor: Vehicles only on roads and lots open to them.
state.hours: DNR lands are closed 11 p.m. to 6 a.m. except to campers and hunters (NR 45.04(2)(a)).
state.cite: Wis. Admin. Code NR 45.04(1s); NR 45.03(9i), (9k) definitions

sna.name: State Natural Area
sna.short: Same as DNR land: edible fruits, edible nuts, wild mushrooms, wild asparagus and watercress, by hand, for personal use. No seeds, roots or other plant parts.
never: Seeds, roots or any other plant parts
sna.cite: Wisconsin DNR, State Natural Areas Program, Wild edibles: What can I collect?

federal.name: Chequamegon-Nicolet National Forest
federal.short: No permit needed to gather edible material (morels and the like) for your own eating. Selling, or larger amounts, needs a permit from the district office.
limits: Ask the Lakewood-Laona district office about anything beyond a small personal amount
federal.motor: Follow the forest's Motor Vehicle Use Map.
federal.cite: USDA Forest Service, Chequamegon-Nicolet NF, Permits: Do you need a pass or permit?

bcpl.name: School trust land (BCPL)
bcpl.short: Open to the public for hunting, fishing, trapping, berry picking and hiking. Mushrooms and plants are not listed, so stick to berries.
limits: Some parcels are surrounded by private land; ask before crossing
bcpl.cite: Wisconsin Board of Commissioners of Public Lands, Public Access

mfl_open.name: Private forest open to the public (Managed Forest Law, open)
mfl_open.short: Walk-in for hunting, fishing, hiking, sightseeing and cross-country skiing only. No picking or gathering unless the owner says yes.
never: Gathering anything without the owner's permission
mfl_open.cite: Wis. Stat. 77.83(2)(a); Wisconsin DNR, Tax Law Lands Open to Public Recreation FAQ

private.name: Private land
private.short: Ask the owner first. Most river and lake banks are private.

general: Never pick a mushroom to eat unless an expert has checked it in person. Wisconsin's deadly mushrooms grow in the same woods.
Take a little and leave the rest: one leaf per ramp plant, a few fiddleheads per crown, berries for the birds.
Hunting seasons: wear blaze orange in fall, especially the November gun deer season.
Ojibwe tribal members exercising treaty gathering rights follow tribal codes and NR 13; this map shows the general public rules.
